title: strkey.Encode emits a signed-payload strkey for an empty payload
severity_basis: Encode side: the SDK produces a P strkey that SEP-23 calls invalid and that its own decoder refuses from v0.7.2. No reader impact verified. Open upstream.

entries.expected: refuse to encode a signed payload of 0 bytes (SEP-23: 1 to 64 bytes)
entries.observed: Executed on v0.7.2, v0.7.3, v0.8.0 and v0.9.0: strkey.Encode emits PA7QYNF7…AAAAAAKH4Y for an empty payload, which the SDK's own decoder then refuses ('signed payload declares 0 payload bytes').

evidence.pre_fix: Conformance runner (xcc conform run --set all), L4, on go@v0.7.1, v0.7.2, v0.7.3, v0.8.0 and v0.9.0.
evidence.expected_basis: SEP-23 v1.4.0: a signed payload carries 1 to 64 bytes; rs-stellar-strkey requires a non-empty payload since #107.

reproduction.method: Independent reviewer reproduction from the record alone on 2026-11-12: 4 of 4 listed report rows failed again as recorded, all offline. Review: findings/review/F-0025.json.

evidence_added.reason: The issue already states this exact asymmetry with the same input; our entry reproduces exactly what it describes, so no new evidence is added.

history.note: Created from the known divergences that reference https://github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/issues/5981 and their failure rows.
The upstream item already records this defect.
